text:
mike: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change landed yesterday, I'm seeing KV-cache growth on long-context repros on MI250X. Memory doesn't trim, and pagetable entries accumulate until OOM. Repro: ./tools/run_repro.sh --model paged-attn --seq 16384 --batch 2 --gpu mi250x --seed 42

tara: thanks, mike. can you paste the top-level perf counters? also which commit?

mike: commit 7f4a2d3 (selector: prefer tiled_kernel for seq>=8192). quick snippet: 
```
KV cache pages allocated: 1.2G -> 3.9G over 1200 steps
pt_walk_async faults/sec: 0.0
pt_walk_sync faults/sec: 480
page_evictions: 0
page_alloc_retries: 12
```

alex: weird that async walk shows 0.0. sounds like we fell back to sync walk and never evicted. could be ordering of pt metadata writes + kernel that expects immediate ownership.

sam: @mike can you run with env KV_DEBUG=1 and kernel debug trace? command: KV_DEBUG=1 KV_TRACE=ptwrite ./build/bin/paged_attn_repro --seq 16384 --batch 2 --gpu mi250x > /tmp/kvtrace.log 2>&1

mike: pasted first 200 lines of /tmp/kvtrace.log: 
```
[0.001] allocate_page page_id=0x7f8a1c size=65536 owner=block_12
[0.045] pt_write page_id=0x7f8a1c owner=block_12 -> committed=false
[0.045] async_kernel matmul_attn_kernel_v2 scheduled on tile0
[0.046] pt_commit page_id=0x7f8a1c owner=block_12 -> committed=true
[0.047] kernel_release expected_owner=block_12 owner_seen=block_34
[0.047] page_stolen page_id=0x7f8a1c new_owner=block_34
```

tara: that kernel_release mismatch looks bad. kernel selected a tiled kernel that runs on a different tile-owner mapping; it seems to read pt entries mid-update. On MI250X we rely on pt writes being visible before kernel uses owner metadata but selector is overlapping async operations.

alex: can confirm: on RTX series the selector chose coalesced_kernel and we didn't hit the race because coalesced_kernel does a prefetch sync. on MI it picks tiled_kernel for perf and that one omits an explicit pt barrier. so race only manifests on MI.

sam: possible mitigations: 1) add an explicit pt memory barrier in tiled_kernel, 2) make selector avoid tiled_kernel if KV writes pending, 3) make pt_write commit synchronous for hot path.

mike: temporary patch applied locally: in kernel selector, avoid tiled_kernel for seq>=8192 on MI*. Re-ran repro: memory growth stabilizes, pt_walk_sync drops to ~60 faults/sec, page_alloc_retries -> 0. perf penalty ~4-6% latency p90.

tara: good quick fix. we should add a unit test fuzz that exercises interleaved pt-write + kernel launch ordering across GPUs. cc @infra-bot for long-running CI job.

infra-bot: scheduled job kv-pagetable-fuzz/mi250x (24h) — will run variations: batch [1,2,4], seq [4096,8192,16384], kernel-selection toggles. Link: https://ci.internal/jobs/kv-pagetable-fuzz/5401239876

alex: followup engineering work: - ensure kernel metadata reads are ordered with pt_commit on all backends - update kernel-selection heuristics to include backend-specific memory-ordering capabilities - add telemetry for "owner_mismatch" to catch early in prod.

sam: also flag for release notes: regression introduced by selector change; add mitigation and rollout plan.

mike: I'll open PR with the selector rollback + test and a follow-up RFC for a more robust pt fencing solution. PR draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/897

tara: thanks. if CI repro reproduces on other MI variants we'll need to coordinate with hw team — paging semantics differ subtly. Let's collect backtraces when owner_mismatch occurs and attach to the issue.

mike: attaching example backtrace from repro: 
```
#0  kernel_release() at runtime/kernel.c:412
#1  tiled_kernel_entry() at kernels/tiled_attn.S:234
#2  launch_kernel() at runtime/launch.c:89
#3  run_paged_attn_step() at runtime/paged_kv.c:678
```

alex: perfect. I'll do a follow-up perf profile to see if adding a barrier can be optimized away in common fastpath.

sam: marking for triage meeting tomorrow. agenda: reproduce matrix, selector rollback risk, perf delta measurement, long-term fencing RFC.

mike: thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated with CI results. :thumbsup:
